newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico Cetes rates soar at end on election nerves.
newsitem.headline: Mexico Cetes rates soar at end on election nerves.

text.p: Interest rates on Mexico's overnight Cetes, or T-bills, jumped 270 basis points to 24 percent at the close of trade on Friday due to growing jitters ahead of upcoming elections.
Dealers said speculation was made worse by a thin market.
"There was not a lot of volume and that's why rates went up so much. A lack of volume is a symptom of volatility," a trader said.

"Elections are the main reason for the nervousness and to a lesser extent the Fed meeting," another dealer said, referring to the July 2 meeting of the Federal Reserve to set U.S. interest rate policy.
Mexicans go to the polls on July 6 to elect most of a new Congress, Mexico City's mayor and six state governors.

Polls in the past few days show Mexico's long-ruling Institutional Revolutionary Party is likely to lose its majority in the lower house of Congress -- something that has not happened in modern Mexico.
Bank notes and acceptances also rose sharply, closing up 230 basis points at 25.35 percent.
